title: Architecting High-Throughput Event Ingestion with Spring WebFlux, Kafka & Automated PII Masking
summary: Building a privacy-compliant MarTech analytics gateway that handles thousands of real-time e-commerce conversion events with sub-second latency.
author: Tan Huynh Nhat

sections.context-problem: During flash sales and peak marketing campaigns, e-commerce traffic surges by 15x–20x. The tracking gateway must reliably capture tens of thousands of customer micro-events per second (cart additions, voucher clicks, product views) and relay them to Google Analytics 4 and Facebook Conversions API. Traditional synchronous architectures caused thread exhaustion and sluggish checkout experiences.
sections.system-requirements:
• Functional: Ingest, validate, cleanse, and route tracking events in real time to external marketing partners.
  • Non-Functional: p99 API response time < 15ms, sustain 10,000 RPS throughput, strict PII privacy compliance (Decree 13/2023/ND-CP), and zero message loss during partner outages.
sections.architecture-design:
We designed an asynchronous, non-blocking Reactive Event-Driven architecture:

  • Ingestion Layer: Spring WebFlux (Project Reactor over Netty) ingests requests asynchronously and immediately buffers payloads to an Apache Kafka cluster.
  • Privacy & Sanitization: Custom Spring AOP interceptors and Jackson serializers recursively mask sensitive PII (emails, phone numbers, identity numbers) using salted SHA-256 hashing.
  • Outbound Delivery: Consumer microservices read from Kafka and dispatch payload batches via non-blocking Spring WebClient.
sections.trade-offs-analysis:
Evaluating Synchronous MVC vs. Reactive WebFlux:

  • Traditional Spring MVC (Thread-per-request): Straightforward debugging, but high concurrency leads to thread starvation and memory bloat under 5,000+ concurrent connections.
  • Reactive Non-Blocking (Spring WebFlux): Steeper learning curve for reactive stream debugging, but scales effortlessly across 20,000+ RPS using minimal CPU threads and 60% less heap memory.
sections.lessons-best-practices: Integrate Resilience4j Circuit Breakers and rate limiters on outbound ad connectors to isolate upstream latency. Never invoke blocking JDBC or file I/O operations directly within the reactive Event Loop.
